title: V4SDDC027 Corporate Mobiles (SIM Cards)
description:
The authority is seeking a capable and innovative supplier to deliver and manage voice and data SIM services across its operations. The solution must support modern connectivity needs, streamline operations, and align with the authority's environmental and social values.\r
\r
Connectivity & Coverage\r
•	Provision of multi-network SIMs that enable seamless switching between providers (e.g., Vodafone, EE) to ensure consistent coverage across South Derbyshire, particularly in low-signal areas.\r
•	Ability to manage multiple cellular network agreements e.g. Vodafone, EE under a single, unified account structure, simplifying billing, reporting, and service coordination.\r
•	Support for Wi-Fi calling and other technologies that enhance mobile availability and reduce reliance on cellular signal alone.\r
Operational Efficiency\r
•	Simplified billing and departmental cost allocation, with automated reporting tools that consolidate multi-network usage.\r
•	Robust self-service capabilities allowing the authority to manage SIMs independently, including activation, suspension, and replacement.\r
Account Management & Support\r
•	A dedicated account management plan that covers all network providers under one umbrella, with clear SLAs, escalation procedures, and proactive service reviews.\r
•	Responsive customer support tailored to the authority's structure and operational needs\r
Environmental & Social Values\r
•	Commitment to energy-efficient operations and reduction of electronic waste through responsible recycling and reuse initiatives.\r
•	Demonstrated community engagement, ethical sourcing practices, and strong data privacy and security compliance.

title: V4SDDC057 LGR Consultancy
description:
Derbyshire's Local Government Reorganisation represents a significant and complex transformation. The programme will require the consolidation of ten councils into a new governance structure of either one unitary or two unitaries.  \r
\r
Outcome 1 - Programme Governance, Planning and Mobilisation\r
The supplier must:\r
•	Utilise the established governance structure and ensure Programme Boards and Programmes are properly constituted and organised from the outset, using PRINCE2/MSP methodology.\r
•	Support the design of a Programme Management Office (PMO) with definition of roles, reporting lines, escalation routes, and decision pathways, including implementation principles.  \r
•	Support in the development of programme documentation including the programme brief and the initial programme strategy and programme plans\r
•	Strengthen programme governance through risk management, dependency tracking, and overall delivery confidence for the Chief Executives' Group and Strategic Leadership Board.\r
•	Provide independent facilitation and structure that supports momentum and consistent collaboration across all ten councils.\r
•	Define Day 1 statutory and operational readiness requirements and produce a single integrated programme plan supporting transition to vesting day.\r
•	Support Programme and Project level (previously workstreams) mobilisation.\r
\r
\r
Outcome 2 - Data Hub\r
The supplier must:\r
•	Design and support the implementation of a centralised data hub including the governance and data architecture to consolidate currently fragmented datasets from all ten councils. Including the provision of data readiness tools, standards and templates.\r
•	Develop a validated service taxonomy to standardise data storage, categorisation and definitions\r
•	Create a unified, trusted evidence base for service redesign, business cases, financial modelling, and transition planning.\r
•	Ensure data consistency for Programme Boards to make informed and timely decisions.\r
•	Identify integration opportunities aligned to MHCLG preparatory activities \r
•	Support in the development of a MoU/Data Sharing Agreement for the implementation phase\r
\r
\r
Outcome 3 - Public Service Reform (PSR) Vision & Transformation Roadmap\r
The supplier must:\r
•	Facilitate design workshops and defining a vision statement\r
•	Define shared principles for reformed service delivery.\r
•	Produce a transformation roadmap aligned to LGR milestones \r
•	Bring real world expertise from previous LGR implementations, ensuring the ten councils follow proven transformation approaches and avoid common pitfalls. \r
•	Provide additional transformation capacity to relieve pressure on senior officers and allow councils to maintain business-as-usual delivery.\r
•	Strengthen cross council collaboration, alignment and culture-building to prepare for the new single or dual unitary arrangements.

title: MH 0071 - Pest Control Services - AWARD
description:
The Contract will mainly be for treatment of Rats, Mice and Cockroaches but on occasion, Midland Heart will need the Contractor to deal with all pests listed below (list not exhaustive) -  
      
      Rats
      Bird mites
      Flies
      Mice
      Lice
      Dust Mites
      Cockroaches
      Fleas
      Ants
      Bed Bugs
      Wasps
      Silverfish
      Squirrels
      Hornets 
      
      The only exceptions are protected species & honeybees (where Midland Heart will decide on how to proceed following advice from the Contractor).
      
      The services will be delivered direct through the Contractors own staff and will not be subcontracted without written permission from Midland Heart.
      
      The above services are required across a range of different stock and tenure's including Void properties, General Needs properties, Retirement and Supported Living properties, Home Options (Leasehold and Shared Ownership) properties and Mutual Properties. 
      
      The Contract is expected to commence on the 6th of March 2023.
      
      Lot 1 - Birmingham, Wolverhampton, Sandwell, Dudley, Wychavon, Herefordshire, Redditch, Bromsgrove, Stroud, Shropshire UA, Swindon, West Oxfordshire, Cotswold, Tewkesbury, Worcester, Wyre Forest and Wiltshire UA.
      
      Lot 2 - Coventry, Leicester, Stoke on Trent, East Staffordshire, Tamworth, Nuneaton and Bedworth, Rugby, Lichfield, Cannock Chase, Northampton Borough Council, North Warwickshire, Hinckley and Bosworth, Charnwood, Walsall, East Northamptonshire, Solihull, Harborough, North West Leicestershire, Blaby, Milton Keynes, Oadby and Wigston, Staffordshire Moorlands, South Staffordshire, Warwick, Broxtowe, Rushcliffe, East Staffordshire, South Kesteven, Newcastle under Lyme, South Derbyshire, Kettering, South Northamptonshire, Wellingborough, Corby Borough Council and Stafford.
      
      Contractors should note, the splits outlined below are indicative only and may be subject to change throughout the life of the Contract.  
      
      Following evaluation of the compliant Tenders Midland Heart shall determine which profile of lot award demonstrates the most economically advantageous outcome and consequently the contract may be awarded to one or multiple contractors (i.e. a minimum of 1 or a maximum of 2).
